case_name: Jagdeep Singh & Anr vs State Of Punjab And Ors

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Punjab and others (government agency)

facts_of_case: Petitioners, a married couple, sought protection from harassment by respondents. Petitioner No.2 was found to be a minor at the time of marriage. The trial court ordered protection for both petitioners.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnised in contravention of some but not all conditions prescribed for valid marriage is not void.
legal_principles.held: Two incontrovertible propositions emerge from a combined reading of Sections 5 and 11 and other provisions of the Act, that the Act specifies conditions for valid marriage and a marriage contracted in breach of some but not all of them renders the marriage void.

legal_principles.principle: The law prescribes conditions for valid marriage and does not leave it to inference that each one of such conditions is mandatory.
legal_principles.held: The statute thus prescribes conditions for valid marriage and also does not leave it to inference that each one of such conditions is mandatory and a contravention, violation or breach of any one of them would be treated as a breach of a prerequisite for a valid marriage rendering it void.

outcome.final_order: Petitioner No.2 was sent to a Protection Home, and respondent No.2 was directed to provide necessary protection to petitioner No.1.
